verifications.claim: Christina Koch is a NASA astronaut.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA astronaut Christina Koch'; R2: 'NASA astronaut Christina Koch'; R3: 'Christina Koch is among four astronauts that are a part of NASA’s Artemis II mission'
verifications.reasoning: All references explicitly identify her as a NASA astronaut.

verifications.claim: As of April 2026, Christina Koch is set to become the first woman to travel around the moon on the Artemis II mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Posted 4/1/2026... Christina Koch will be the first woman on a moon mission... Artemis II mission, which will travel around the moon'; R2: 'In April... Artemis II mission... Koch will become the first female to travel to the moon'; R3: 'Artemis II mission... first woman around the moon'
verifications.reasoning: All references confirm the April 2026 timeline and describe Koch as the first woman on the moon mission that travels around the moon.

verifications.claim: Christina Koch is a mission specialist on the Artemis II mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'One of those crew members is Christina Koch, who will be a mission specialist.'
verifications.reasoning: R2 directly states her role as mission specialist on Artemis II.

verifications.claim: Christina Koch is a veteran astronaut.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'set another record earlier in her career... spent 328 days in space'; R2: 'spent more than 300 days in space to set her previous record'; R3: 'the (woman who has spent the longest time in space)'
verifications.reasoning: References describe her extensive prior experience and records but do not use the term 'veteran'; support is indirect through her history.

verifications.claim: Christina Koch has previously spent the longest time in space by a woman.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'setting the record for the longest continuous spaceflight by a woman'; R2: 'Koch broke it... Koch spent more than 300 days'; R3: 'the (woman who has spent the longest time in space)'
verifications.reasoning: All references explicitly confirm she holds/held the record for longest spaceflight by a woman.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is around the moon, not landing.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'travel around the moon and back... key step toward a long-term return to the Moon'; R3: 'going on the other side of the moon... around the moon'; R2 implies orbital as no landing mentioned
verifications.reasoning: References describe the mission as traveling around the moon without mentioning landing, contrasting with future return/landing plans.

verifications.claim: The Apollo era had all-male crews.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'all of the astronauts were men.'
verifications.reasoning: R2 directly states all Apollo moon mission astronauts were men.

verifications.claim: Previous reports discussed plans to walk on the moon.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No references mention previous reports or specific plans to walk on the moon.

verifications.claim: The initial 2026 Artemis II mission aims to orbit the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first crewed moon mission... in more than 50 years... travel around the moon' (April 2026); R2: 'In April... return to the moon with astronauts'; R3: 'Artemis II mission'
verifications.reasoning: References confirm 2026 Artemis II as first crewed mission orbiting/around the moon.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission makes Christina Koch the first woman to reach the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first woman on a moon mission'; R2: 'first female to travel to the moon'; R3: 'first woman to travel to the moon... first woman around the moon'
verifications.reasoning: All references state Koch is the first woman on/to the moon via Artemis II.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is a crewed flight
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first crewed moon mission... four astronauts aboard'; R2: 'astronauts on the Artemis II mission'; R3: 'four astronauts that are a part of NASA’s Artemis II mission'
verifications.reasoning: All references explicitly describe Artemis II as crewed with astronauts aboard.
